name: Do I need to move out during a room addition?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to move out during a room addition in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Do I need to move out during a room addition in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether you need to move out depends on the size and location of the project. If the addition is isolated from the rest of the home and utilities can stay active, some families remain in place. Larger projects, especially second-story additions, major structural work, or additions that affect bathrooms, kitchens, or primary access points, can make living at home difficult. Noise, dust, contractor traffic, and utility shutoffs are the main reasons people temporarily relocate. Homeowners should ask the contractor how the site will be secured, which rooms will be unavailable, and whether water, power, or HVAC will be interrupted. If staying home is possible, create a clear plan for barriers, daily cleanup, and safe access routes. If the project is large, the cost of temporary housing should be considered part of the total budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not always, but some homeowners move out during major additions because of noise, dust, safety issues, and temporary loss of utilities or access. Smaller additions may allow you to stay in the home if the work area can be properly separated from living spaces.
